7. Why is method overloading called compile-time polymorphism?
Method overloading is called compile-time polymorphism because the compiler determines which overloaded method is suitable during compilation, based on the method call and its arguments.
It is called polymorphism because the same method name, add, is used with different parameter lists or forms.
8. Why is method overloading called early binding?
means connecting a method call to the method that should execute.
Method overloading is called early binding because the appropriate overloaded method is selected during compilation, before the program executes.
The compiler determines the overloaded method first, so the binding happens early.

Runtime polymorphism occurs when a method call is resolved to the appropriate overridden instance method during program execution.

15. Why is method overriding called runtime polymorphism?
Method overriding is called runtime polymorphism because the JVM determines which overridden instance-method implementation executes at runtime, based on the actual object.
For example, if a parent reference points to a child object, the call executes the child's overridden method.
Overloading: compiler selects the method during compilation.
Overriding: JVM dispatches the call to the appropriate implementation at runtime.
Late binding means the method implementation is determined at runtime rather than being fully selected during compilation.
For overridden instance methods, the JVM uses the actual object's class to determine which implementation should execute.

25. Why are warnings important in Java?
A warning does not always prevent a program from compiling or executing, but it can indicate code that should be reviewed.
In real applications, developers should investigate warnings rather than automatically ignoring them, because warnings can point to code-quality or reliability concerns.
